caseHighlights.title: Measured macrorealism class exclusion, not multiverse evidence · S-002-R011
caseHighlights.summary: Knee et al. 2016 full original main article: superconducting flux qubit 170 nA / roughly 10 ns, calibrated disturbances d_g=-0.026612, d_e=+0.015884 and d_rho=-0.089788, our published-number significance 83.91 sigma. Physically rejects specified mixture-control macrorealist models, yet standard Everett and Bohmian equilibrium agree.
caseHighlights.limitation: No raw event trials/supplement; 84-sigma pertains to experiment's operational macrorealist Eq7 class only, not Everett vs Bohm or original GRW parameter exclusion.

caseHighlights.title: S-002-R008 quantitative CSL replication, common rC reference
caseHighlights.summary: Ge count-level Gamma 95% posterior λ<5.1973e-13/s independently computed (source 5.2e-13); LISA 2024 acceleration PSD Eq10 λ<8.364e-11/s (source 8.3e-11), both at rC 1e-7m. XENON published 90%-CL model ratio converts to λ<3e-17 but full nuisance likelihood not reproduced; molecule and rotational numeric curves not invented.
caseHighlights.limitation: Independent summary-input math not independent experimental data; exact Ge double pseudocount, Bayesian vs frequentist vs conservative PSD, opposite rc scaling and correlated LISA data are essential. Physical history ontology unresolved; neutral editorial 50.

caseHighlights.title: Ten original main-paper tests and adversarial checks · R006
caseHighlights.summary: Fein molecular interference; Donadi 124kg-day germanium X-rays; shared-LISA force/torque reanalyses; colored CSL, inflation operator, classical-gravity entanglement and Wigner-friend conditional counterarguments. New MOVE-002–007 model-specific constraints; central histories score neutral 50.
caseHighlights.limitation: Whole accessible main texts reviewed; not raw experimental-data or all supplemental-proofs replication; correlated LISA evidence not independently counted.

caseHighlights.title: Real experimental result: benchmark Markovian CSL parameter region constrained · S-002-R005
caseHighlights.summary: XENONnT 2026 complete main paper reports 90%-CL λ/rC²<3×10^-3 s^-1 m^-2 and 9.1σ deviation of historical GRW-associated benchmark when specified as white-noise CSL. Strong experimental progress for collapse physics, not a direct Everett-versus-Bohm branch census.
caseHighlights.limitation: Full original 7-page main XENONnT letter examined, but supplementary signal derivations and raw-event likelihood not independently replicated; historical 59→50 is baseline repair, not evidence for one physical history.

caseHighlights.title: Everett 1957 original main text critically reviewed · S-002-R003
caseHighlights.summary: Everett's §5 note added in proof calls all branch elements actual inside the theory; §§4–5 derive relative records and an additive squared-amplitude measure. Mathematical branch weights plus observers' coherent memories still do not empirically identify alternative real histories.
caseHighlights.limitation: Original main paper read in retypeset copy rather than verified publisher facsimile; independent full proof/empirical reproduction absent; original 59 was later reset to neutral editorial 50; actual number of physical histories unresolved.

caseHighlights.title: S-002-R001 · Four-theory quantitative observational comparison
caseHighlights.summary: Everett and equilibrium Bohmian mechanics yield the same ordinary Born distribution while describing different actual histories. GRW/CSL differs only when physical collapse changes predicted observables. See detailed 2×2 decoherence and parameterized GRW toy.
caseHighlights.limitation: Only original Bohm I/II and 2016 Hensen are newly fully main-text reviewed. Other foundational and 2026 bound originals are abstracts/targeted passages; no experiment reproduced.

caseHighlights.title: Quantum reality after a measurement

caseHighlights.limitation: No unique evidence for physical branch count.

caseHighlights.title: Hawking: formation restrictions
caseHighlights.summary: Compactly generated Cauchy horizons arising from a bounded intervention face energy-condition obstacles and semiclassical vacuum-polarization concerns.
caseHighlights.limitation: A conditional argument, not a universal theorem about quantum gravity.

caseHighlights.title: Kay–Radzikowski–Wald: precise theorem
caseHighlights.summary: At certain horizon base points, standard linear-field algebra and regular Hadamard state extension cannot satisfy the stipulated local requirements.
caseHighlights.limitation: A field-theory mathematical obstruction, not a direct stress-tensor measurement or proof of no time travel.

caseHighlights.title: Visser: semiclassical reliability
caseHighlights.summary: Short closed spacelike paths and metric fluctuations may place the chronology horizon beyond where semiclassical gravity can be trusted.
caseHighlights.limitation: This undermines overconfident extrapolation; it does not create a time machine.

journal.title: A physical measurement narrows macrorealism without counting worlds
journal.intro: A complete five-page original superconducting-qubit article and independent published-error propagation produce a genuine approximately 84-standard-deviation test of a specified nonclassical-disturbance bound. This improves what Worldline can reject, not its ability to count physical histories.

sections.heading: An experimental definition matters
sections.text: Knee et al. 2016 define an operational macrorealist disturbance inequality: a coherent preparation may not disturb a future measurement more than the range observed for two definite pointer preparations. With an independently applied blind pulse, this bound is experimentally testable.

sections.heading: Reproducing the stated significance
sections.text: Published g/e/coherent disturbance means are -0.026612, +0.015884 and -0.089788. The coherent minus g gap -0.063176 divided by 0.00075286 in combined source-rounded uncertainty gives 83.91 standard deviations. Under the defined control-model class, a strong physical result.

sections.heading: Not an Everett branch observation
sections.text: The main paper itself allows different hidden-state preparation behavior as an escape from its convex-mixture bound. Everett and Bohmian quantum equilibrium both predict ordinary quantum coherence. A rejection of this macrorealism subclass therefore cannot favor many actual timelines over one actual Bohmian configuration.

sections.heading: Scope of the completed review
sections.text: Five full original pages, Fig1–3, control procedures, equations and published errors studied; supplementary figures and author-held raw trial data not reconstructed. Historic GRW original remains an abstract/targeted reading until its full 22 pages can be accessed.

journal.title: Testing the one-real-history question with Born-rule anomalies
journal.intro: Two complete original-source reviews distinguish proposals that could discriminate physical models from familiar Born measurements that cannot separate the Everett and equilibrium Bohm ontologies.

sections.heading: A falsifiable polarization deviation
sections.text: Valentini and Varma model a nonlinear polarization-axis probability from specified pilot-wave nonequilibrium. Their illustrative 1% deviation needs at least 360000 usable ideal photons for 3-sigma sensitivity at pi/8; with 80% signal fraction the sample estimate becomes about 562500. Existing directly top-radiated photons are far fewer, and adequate individual gamma-ray polarization analysis remains unavailable.

sections.heading: The measured tau sample does not reject Born statistics
sections.text: The paper cites CMS tau helicity -0.144±0.015, versus -0.1472±0.0016 expected, approximately 0.21 standard deviations apart in a simplified Gaussian comparison. The analysis is not a new collider discovery, and background/event-selection algorithms may assume the very Born rule under test.

sections.heading: What one actual configuration predicts
sections.text: Norsen compares Born-rule emergence via quantum equilibrium typicality and dynamical relaxation. A Bohmian one-configuration equilibrium account and an Everett unitary Born-weighted account make the same standard pointer-record probabilities; their likelihood ratio is 1 for those matched experiments.

sections.heading: Decision and limitations
sections.text: Full papers read and source-linked; no raw CMS/ATLAS detector fit or Norsen simulation independently rerun. WL-019 records a proposed distinguishing model test and why the central editorial 50 is unchanged. The R010 five-round content review checks all eight routes; direct mobile/browser navigation still requires separate acceptance.

journal.title: What would actually change one history versus many?
journal.intro: Our highest scientific priority is to identify measurements where fully specified single-history and multiple-history models disagree, rather than simply cataloguing compatible quantum results.

sections.heading: Why the CSL calculations matter, but are indirect
sections.text: Germanium/XENON/LISA/molecule bounds constrain possible single-outcome collapse laws. Some such mechanisms are disfavored, but quantum-equilibrium Bohmian dynamics can still have one actual result while matching Everett standard Born observations.

sections.heading: The same experiment can seem to favor opposite claims without a fixed model
sections.text: With Ge 576 counts and fixed simulated background 506, a preselected weak CSL signal and an overly strong signal give opposite Poisson likelihood ratios relative to no signal. Selecting a model parameter after observing data is cherry-picking. Full background uncertainty and a prior over parameter families are required before using it to adjust a numerical central score.

sections.heading: Highest impact research targets
sections.text: Derive Everett/Bohmian equilibrium operational equivalence; investigate falsifiable Born-rule deviations in high-energy collision polarization, controlled recoherence of durable measurement records versus physical collapse, and adversarial Wigner-friend assumptions.

sections.heading: Five-round website freshness
sections.text: Session decision is recorded every research round. Every five rounds all eight pages receive evidence-linked source checks and refresh or justified no-change, with the next full sweep at S-002-R010.

journal.title: Independently reconstructing experimental collapse-model bounds
journal.intro: Two previously reported CSL parameter limits are now directly computed in Worldline Lab from original paper formulas and published aggregate data, with full source-statistic distinctions and an explicit correction of a one-count inference offset.

sections.heading: Germanium: an independently evaluated Bayesian 95% bound
sections.text: For 576 detected photons, 506 simulated background counts, signal coefficient 2.0986, and the source-defined +1 for BOTH signal and background components, the 95th Gamma(577,1) total-mean quantile is 617.071. Subtracting 508 and converting at rC=1e-7 m gives lambda upper 5.1973e-13/s, reproducing the printed 5.2e-13. This conditions on the background/efficiency model; it is not a raw detector reanalysis.

sections.heading: LISA: SI acceleration-noise reconstruction and independent geometry
sections.text: For 1.928kg, cube width 46mm, density 19,881kg/m3 and the paper's February 2017 Brownian PSD uncertainty 0.075 fm²s^-4/Hz, Eq10 yields lambda upper 8.364e-11/s, agreeing with the source 8.3e-11. The asymptotic translational upper curve scales inversely with rC², opposite to the X-ray curves. This is not a 90% or 95% bound.

sections.heading: Different instruments, no forced joint likelihood
sections.text: XENON's published 90% white-noise CSL bound converts to lambda<3e-17/s at rC=1e-7m, but its original full 9.1sigma nuisance-background likelihood was not rerun; the molecule-fringe and LISA-torque curves remain source-reported but not independently calculated. Don't combine these confidence rules as if independent equal-probability measurements. Ledger MOVE-008 records increased computational trust, not new physical branch observations.

journal.title: Ten high-impact papers move physical claims, not unearned points
journal.intro: Ten complete original main-text critical readings span genuine molecular and germanium measurements, LISA noise reanalyses, colored collapse-law escape routes and rigorous counterexamples to interpretation claims.

sections.heading: Real measurement changes
sections.text: Measured 25±3% molecular interference fringe example and 124kg-day germanium X-ray search constrain specified objective-collapse models. Two distinct LISA analyses are based on the same spacecraft data and are not independent experiments.

sections.heading: Why specific experiments are decisive
sections.text: Each finding has a named generator, geometry, detector frequency range, null/alternative and caveat. Colored CSL spectra and alternate gravity-matter channels limit over-generalizing tests.

sections.heading: What would answer the original question?
sections.text: A measured likelihood ratio separating one physically realized history from Everett multiple real branches under matched physical preparations, or a rigorous demonstration that an experiment cannot identify them. None of the ten constitutes an observed branch census.

journal.title: Why 59 was unjustified—and what actually moved the evidence
journal.intro: The original +9 editorial tilt toward many histories lacked a documented scientific derivation. A neutral 50 editorial anchor restores fairness, while a complete primary-paper reading makes a quantitative experimental constraint visible without treating it as proof of many worlds.

sections.heading: The score was an assumption, not a conclusion
sections.text: Early Worldline Lab imported 59 from an earlier planning discussion even after changing the central question. VC-010 corrects that unsupported preference to neutral 50. The correction is methodological, not new evidence supporting one-world or a 50% probability.

sections.heading: Scientific progress can genuinely eliminate a physical parameter region
sections.text: The 2026 XENONnT paper studied a measured 1–140 keV recoil spectrum and reported a 90%-CL limit λ/rC²<3.0×10^-3 s^-1m^-2 for white-noise Markovian CSL. In that CSL model the historical GRW parameter pair lies 9.1σ away from the best fit, as reported by the collaboration. That meaningfully restricts one outcome-selection dynamical mechanism.

sections.heading: Why the number of actual histories remains a different question
sections.text: Everettian unitary branches and quantum-equilibrium Bohm with one actual configuration predict matching Born experiments. Excluding one collapse parameter does not decide their ontology. The scientific ledger now records model-specific moves separately, and further work must seek an actual differentiating likelihood or demonstrate the identifiable limitation.

journal.title: Everett's claim of actual branches and why it is not a branch census
journal.intro: The 1957 primary paper explicitly treats every uncollapsed component as actual in the proposed theory. Its additive measure yields Born weights under assumptions; another theory with one actual configuration reproduces the same ordinary probabilities.

sections.heading: One wave function, multiple relative records
sections.text: A universal unitary quantum state can correlate observer memories with all relative outcomes. Everett's §5 proof-note says the components are all actual in that framework. The scientific question remains which ontology describes our actual physical universe.

sections.heading: Why additivity matters but does not finish probability
sections.text: Everett's positive additive measure yields squared-amplitude weights and typical repeated-memory records, but a measure on hypothetical branches does not alone prove their existence or why a particular observer should expect one future experience.

sections.heading: Next engineering and science work
sections.text: The roadmap's Truth Engine v0.2 requires data integrity, counterevidence, explicit score-change provenance and tests, while already implemented v0.25 reading rooms need acceptance revalidation. The planned scientific work is three parts for each part website development.

journal.title: Two histories of the same measurement?
journal.intro: Everett and Bohmian quantum equilibrium disagree about which histories physically exist while agreeing on standard experimental frequencies.

sections.heading: Ontology is not automatically an observable
sections.text: Everett's unitary global wave has multiple branch-relative records. Bohmian mechanics assigns one actual guided particle configuration. Given quantum equilibrium, both yield the same Born measurement statistics.

sections.heading: Where predictions really can differ
sections.text: GRW and CSL change the physical dynamics. Size and time-dependent loss of interference or spontaneous X-ray emission may constrain a specified localization mechanism; environmental decoherence is a major alternative that must be calibrated.

sections.heading: A measured constraint, not a parallel-universe photograph
sections.text: March 2026 XENONnT 1–140 keV results constrain particular Markovian CSL/DP parameter choices. Bell tests constrain locality assumptions. Neither measures the number of actually real Everett branches.

sections.heading: Our open conclusion
sections.text: Three newly completed full original-main-text critical reviews bring the indexed completed total to 13 of 400. The objective is scientific discrimination, not a higher review count; VC-008 leaves 59/100 as an inherited editorial orientation, not a probability.

journal.category: FULL-SOURCE RESEARCH · R006 · TEN COMPLETE STUDIES
journal.title: Ten full scientific reviews: what original research establishes about timelines
journal.intro: The first ten critical main-text source studies are complete. Their conclusions constrain local hidden-variable theories, wavefunction ontology, chronology horizons, quantum causal operations and inflationary bubble detection—but none directly counts real quantum branches.

sections.heading: The main milestone: 10 of 400 full-source reviews
sections.text: We studied whole original main publications or the complete scholarly entry, and logged their sections, methods, assumptions, limitations, independent checks and competing explanations. Nine previously indexed works and one new single-world paper were promoted; no abstract-only work was relabeled merely to raise the counter.

sections.heading: 1. Bell and PBR: strong theorems, narrow conclusions
sections.text: Bell's 1964 original demonstrates the nonlocality constraint on precise preassignment models. PBR's full paper and appendices restrict overlapping ψ-epistemic descriptions under independent preparation. Neither theorem asserts that Everettian branches were directly observed.

sections.heading: 2. Many-worlds theory alongside a substantive single-world response
sections.text: Vaidman's full 2026 scholarly treatment explains branch ontology, Born-weight and preferred-basis objections. Lazarovici and Hubert's complete rebuttal addresses a Wigner's-friend paradox using Bohmian definite particle configurations and still-live empty wave branches. They disagree about ontology and do not provide a new branch detector.

sections.heading: 3. Quantum causal order and a Bell-Wigner experiment
sections.text: Oreshkov's process-matrix paper yields a theoretical causal-inequality violation. Procopio's optical quantum switch demonstrates a controlled ordering advantage; Proietti's six-photon Bell-Wigner experiment violates an observer-independent-facts inequality with explicit fair-sampling and observer-definition limitations. These different results must never be counted as direct observation of parallel physical timelines.

sections.heading: 4. Cosmology, rotating metrics and time-loop formation
sections.text: Feeney's complete five-page WMAP analysis uses matched simulations and Bayesian evidence to constrain detectable bubble collisions. Gödel's four-page paper constructs an exact rotating metric with closed timelike circles. Hawking's full original paper investigates restrictions on manufactured chronology horizons. None is evidence for quantum branching in our actual universe.

sections.heading: Math checks and what remains unverified
sections.text: Limited independent checks included CHSH singlet 2√2, PBR two-qubit exclusion orthogonality, Gödel's radius asinh(1), the causal-success value (2+√2)/4, and Proietti's reported significance. Entire experimental datasets, external appendices and full general-relativistic tensor calculations were not independently reproduced. Complete details, source URLs and caveats are in research/full-study-batch-001.md.

sections.heading: The empirical verdict did not move
sections.text: Our central question remains unresolved: one experienced outcome is not an experimental count of all physically real histories. The inherited 59/100 meter is an editorial display rather than calibrated posterior. Research audit VC-007 records 59 to 59 with zero evidential branch-count shift. Next, work on original Everett and Bohm papers, objective-collapse experimental constraints and a quantitative discrimination matrix.

journal.category: RESEARCH REPORT · R005 · ONE REAL HISTORY OR MANY
journal.title: Does our universe contain one timeline—or many physically real histories?
journal.intro: The central problem is the number of actual outcome histories in our own universe, not whether people can revisit the past.

sections.heading: 1 · Everett and relative-state branches
sections.text: Everett interprets one universal uncollapsed quantum state as encompassing many branch-relative worlds. No other actual branch has been directly counted. SRC-007, SRC-012, NOTE-026.

sections.heading: 2 · Decoherence and the quantum cat
sections.text: Environmental entanglement suppresses locally visible interference but does not decide whether a single outcome or multiple branch-relative histories are physically actual. SRC-011, SRC-058, NOTE-027.

sections.heading: 3 · Bohm's one actual configuration
sections.text: Nonlocal particle guidance assigns definite actual positions while reproducing many quantum results, showing that generic interference alone does not demand many actual histories. SRC-010, SRC-059, NOTE-028.

sections.heading: 4 · GRW collapse and molecular experiments
sections.text: Physical-collapse modifications have parameter-dependent predictions. Large-molecule quantum interference constrains some, not all, modified models. SRC-042, SRC-048, NOTE-029.

sections.heading: 5 · Bell tests do not count timelines
sections.text: Loophole-free Bell experiments reject specified local-realist models, not nonlocal single-outcome physics as a category or Everett-vs-Bohm ontology. SRC-060, SRC-061, NOTE-030.

sections.heading: 6 · Separate cosmological bubble hypotheses
sections.text: Eternal-inflation bubbles are physically different from Everett branches. WMAP bubble-collision data showed no warrant for additional model complexity under the tested scenario. SRC-062, SRC-063, NOTE-031.

sections.heading: 7 · PBR's narrower conclusion
sections.text: Wavefunction ontic-status constraints under preparation independence do not prove many actual histories. SRC-044, NOTE-032.

sections.heading: Verdict and continuation
sections.text: One observed history is consistent with competing ontologies. No decisive physical history-count experiment; editorial compass stays 59→59, VC-006. More detailed mathematical and experimental comparisons are next.

journal.title: What chronology protection actually proves—and what it cannot yet prove
journal.intro: A rigorous quantum-field theorem can show that a mathematical description breaks down at specified horizon points without establishing what complete quantum gravity will do.

sections.heading: Hawking's bounded-region scenario
sections.text: Hawking's local construction analysis concerns compactly generated Cauchy horizons, geometric energy conditions and semiclassical vacuum polarization. The backreaction conclusion remains a conditional physical conjecture; it does not eliminate every imaginable closed timelike path.

sections.heading: The precise Kay–Radzikowski–Wald result
sections.text: For a linear field on a spacetime with a compactly generated horizon, specified base points obstruct the usual F-local field algebra and regular Hadamard two-point extension. Even where stress looks bounded before the horizon, the limiting quantum field description can become ill-defined at those base points.

sections.heading: Visser's reliability objection
sections.text: Visser argues semiclassical gravity can cease to be trustworthy because of Planck-scale metric fluctuations before a chronology horizon; a Roman-ring toy geometry also challenges reliance on universally large mean stress. Neither result creates physical time travel.

sections.heading: Evidence verdict
sections.text: The experimental question remains open. This theoretical comparison does not independently detect backward travel or discriminate single-history and many-histories ontology. The site's illustrative 59/100 editorial score stays unchanged; see field-note-003, SOURCE-055–057 and audit VC-005.

sections.heading: Later editorial correction (22 October 2026)
sections.text: This is an archived research-journal entry. Its historic 59/100 reference was an inherited editorial preference, withdrawn at audit VC-010 and reset to a neutral 50 reference that is not a 50% probability. The current main question is one physically realized history or physically real multiple branches; chronology protection alone cannot decide that.

journal.title: The problem is not the grandfather. It is the meaning of a history.
journal.intro: The grandfather paradox is a warning against combining incompatible assumptions. It is not evidence that the cosmos forks.

sections.heading: Three distinct questions
sections.text: Can a clock traverse time at a different rate? Can a physical observer return to an earlier event? If quantum theory branches, are these branches independent histories? The first is experimentally supported; the others remain open.

sections.heading: An evidence discipline
sections.text: A mathematical solution is not a physical device. A quantum simulation is not a journey to yesterday. A philosophical interpretation is not an observation of parallel timelines.

sections.heading: Our research standard
sections.text: Every claim is connected to a dated source, an evidence category, a relevance judgment and a clearly stated limitation. Only findings that distinguish competing accounts can move an empirical verdict.
